research_scope: TikTok and Instagram official API fit plus one cloud vendor, Apify; documentation only.

sources.title: TikTok Research Tools FAQ
claims: Commercial users are not eligible for Research Tools.
A developer account alone does not grant research access.
sources.decision: not appropriate for this commercial selection project
sources.note: Search displayed September 1 but opened body displayed August 4; opened body date retained.

sources.title: Display API Get Started
claims: Requires developer account, product/scope approvals and user authorization.
Retrieves authorized user profile and video metadata; examples include IDs, descriptions and share URLs.
sources.decision: authorized-account supplement; no broad trends capability established

sources.title: Commercial Content API
claims: Application required; commercial-content search includes advertiser/keyword-based queries.
Retrieved page explicitly says EU-only data in current phase.
sources.decision: does not establish US organic-demand coverage

sources.title: Meta official Postman team
claims: Page has a verified badge, identifies itself as the official Meta team, and links an official Instagram API workspace.

sources.title: Instagram API Documentation
claims: Facebook Login API serves professional accounts, requires a linked Page and access token, and supports hashtagged media plus basic metadata/metrics of other professional accounts.
Documented comment management concerns own media.
Instagram Login also serves professional accounts; no whole-platform trend endpoint established.

sources.action: stopped requesting these developer-doc paths; used verified Meta Postman publication

sources.title: Actors
claims: Actors are serverless cloud programs with structured JSON input/output, runnable through API, CLI or schedules.
sources.inference: Cloud Actor execution does not depend on a local Chrome extension connection.

sources.title: TikTok Scraper
claims: Inputs include keywords, hashtags, profiles and video URLs.
Examples contain id, webVideoUrl, createTimeISO, text, playCount, diggCount, shareCount, commentCount and collectCount.

sources.title: TikTok Scraper input
claims: proxyCountryCode controls proxy country/availability, with US among options.
Profile date filters are charged and work with latest/oldest sorting, not popular.
Video search supports relative date filters including PAST_WEEK; search filters are charged.
commentsPerPost stores a linked comment dataset; desired reply completeness is not guaranteed.
sources.inference: Proxy country is not an audience residence or consumer market filter; relative week cannot alone reproduce the fixed window.

sources.title: Instagram Scraper
claims: Supports selected public Instagram URLs/searches, posts, reels, hashtags, profiles, places and comments.
Examples include ID, URL, caption, timestamp, likesCount, commentsCount and selected comment text/timestamps.

sources.title: Instagram Scraper input
claims: Search can target hashtags, profiles or places; comments mode requires post URLs.
onlyPostsNewerThan supports dates/ISO/relative values in UTC; pinned posts may still appear.
Free usage is limited for comments; selected plan affects access and limits.
sources.inference: Place search does not establish US audience/consumer scope; output timestamps still need fixed-window filtering.

sources.title: Instagram Scraper API in Python
claims: Programmatic access requires Apify account and API token.
Example runs the Actor and reads results from its dataset.

sources.title: TikTok Comments Scraper
claims: Selected-video comments include text, timestamp, likes and replies; example includes cid, createTimeISO and videoWebUrl.

recommended_pilot_candidate.recommendation_basis: documented cloud API, maintained labels, source URLs/IDs/time fields and suitable query inputs
recommended_pilot_candidate.history_rule: Current counters on historical posts do not reconstruct historical growth. Use repeated comparable snapshots or a verified historical series.

scope_limit: One vendor only; no Exolyt evaluation was needed. Provider documentation is not a guarantee of data completeness, platform permission or this project's commercial results.
